title: Model Binding
blurb: Every action parameter gets its value from somewhere — the route, the query string, the body, a header. Under [ApiController] there are default conventions. Trace where each value binds.

levels.title: L1 · Default conventions
levels.prompt: No binding attributes are present. Under [ApiController], where does `id` come from?

blocks.label: Action
blocks.code:
[HttpGet("items/{id}")]
public Item Get(int id, string? q)

failStates.title: `q` is the query one
failStates.explain: Simple types bind from the route first when the template has a matching token. `id` matches the {id} route token; `q` (no token) is what binds from the query string.

failStates.title: Simple types don't bind from the body
failStates.explain: Under [ApiController], only a complex type binds from the body. Simple types like int come from the route or query — here `id` matches the {id} route token.

levels.title: L2 · Complex types
levels.prompt: A complex parameter with no attribute, under [ApiController]. Where does `order` bind from?

failStates.title: Complex types default to the body
failStates.explain: Under [ApiController], a complex type with no attribute is inferred as [FromBody]. It deserializes from the JSON body, not the query string.

failStates.title: It binds fine here
failStates.explain: [ApiController] infers [FromBody] for complex types, so the JSON deserializes into order. (Without [ApiController] it would try form/query and come back empty — a classic gotcha.)

levels.title: L3 · Two bodies
levels.prompt: What happens when an action asks for two [FromBody] parameters?

blocks.label: Action

options.label: Runtime error — only one body allowed

failStates.title: A request has only one body
failStates.explain: The body stream can be read once. Two [FromBody] parameters is an invalid configuration — ASP.NET Core throws at runtime rather than guessing.

failStates.title: It doesn't silently half-bind
failStates.explain: It's not 'first wins' — two [FromBody] parameters is an error. Combine them into one model, or read the second value from another source.
